claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in equiatomic multiprincipal-element alloys are governed by a sequential oxidation mechanism involving initial selective oxidation followed by compositional inversion.
Equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn is an exemplar alloy for the proposed mechanism.
The initial CoCrFeNiMn alloy is single-phase and has a homogeneous microstructure.
Initial oxidation stages in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn are governed by atomic size and redox potential.
Elements with lower redox potentials and smaller atomic radii preferentially oxidize first.
Redox potential becomes dominant over time and causes oxide-film composition inversion in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn.
Initial selective oxidation produces a continuous, nanostructured protective oxide layer.
The oxide film is speciated and layered.
The oxide layer remains intact and self-healing while its composition inverts.
The initially formed oxide is dense and adherent, thereby limiting oxygen ingress.
Self-limiting oxide growth slows further oxidation.
The protective oxidation mechanism reduces mechanical degradation and preserves long-term material integrity.
Reducing Cr or Mn disrupts the balance of redox-potential and atomic-size effects.
An unaltered equiatomic alloy will have better oxidation resistance and mechanical integrity than a variant with reduced Cr or Mn.
A compositionally modified alloy will form a less continuous and more heterogeneous oxide and will degrade faster than the equiatomic alloy.
The proposed governing behavior should occur at about 900°C and remain effective up to around 1000°C.
The mechanism should hold generally for equiatomic or near-equiatomic multiprincipal-element alloys between roughly 800°C and 1000°C in oxygen environments.
The mechanism may cease to be effective at lower temperatures or under oxidizing conditions outside the tested oxygen-partial-pressure range.
Atom probe tomography, transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy can track oxidation-induced compositional and structural evolution in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn.

contradictions.description: The conditions call the equiatomic composition the baseline and the altered composition the variant, whereas the baseline field defines the altered, lower-Cr or lower-Mn alloy as the baseline. The predicted outcome again treats the unaltered equiatomic alloy as the reference, leaving the baseline designation inconsistent.
